1 missing] [2] Having empowered a great solar disc measuring one thousand [yojanas], he sat in its center. Then all the Blessed Tathāgatas, having again assembled, made this request to the Lord of all Tathāgatas:
"Excellent for you, O Vajradharma! Excellent for you, O Vajranetra!"
“Excellent for you, O Vajra-knowledge! Excellent for you, O Buddha-knowledge! [and so forth].
Then all the Blessed Tathāgatas, having prostrated to the Blessed Mahāvajradhara, spoke thus:
“We entreat you, O Protector who brings benefit to all Buddhas.”
O Lord, teach the supreme vehicle, the system of the Mahāyāna.
Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi spoke thus to all the Tathāgatas:
"O Blessed Ones, all you Tathāgatas, I am not able to explain the method of the supreme reality.
All the Tathāgatas said:
"What is the cause?
Vajradhara replied:

"O Blessed Ones, all Tathāgatas, there are great Bodhisattvas headed by Maitreya in this very great maṇḍala of the assembly who, upon hearing this supreme method of the Great Mahāyāna ultimate truth, will shatter into a thousand pieces."
All the Tathāgatas said:
"O Lord, you have performed the peaceful consecration for the Buddhas;
one should perform that very same consecration for the Vajras."

Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, with eyes wide open, gave his approval to all the Tathāgatas; having filled the great wheel of all the Tathāgatas with rays of light, he entered the samādhi called "The Exhortation of the Heart of All Tathāgatas. Immediately upon his entering it, four great solar disks appeared.
In the eastern direction, a great solar disk named Akṣayarūpadhārī appeared. In the southern direction, a great solar disk named Ratnacintāmaṇivajra appeared.
In the western direction, a great solar mandala named Amṛtavajra appeared;
in the northern direction, a great solar mandala named Amoghasamayavajra appeared.

Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi taught the Great Kalparāja named *Advayasamatāvijaya* (The Victory of Non-dual Equality) for all the Tathāgatas and all the Bodhisattvas. This is called the *Vajracaryābhiyukta* (Engaged in Vajra Conduct) of all the Tathāgatas. Thus, that very Blessed One Vajrapāṇi dwells in the ten directions together with a retinue-circle endowed with such qualities, by means of such supernatural power distinguished by such qualities.

It is just as if the triple-thousand great thousandfold world-system were completely covered by the light of fireflies; it would not be able to produce even a particle's worth of light in the presence of the radiance of the solar disc. In the same way, all the Tathāgatas became lusterless and remained shrouded in gloom by the radiance of Vajrasattva.

Then all the Blessed Tathāgatas, having worshipped the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi with clouds of offerings to all the Tathāgatas, gave him the name Samantabhadra and remained silent. Then Samantabhadra, the Great Vajradhara, having placed all the Bodhisattvas within his own heart, entered into his own samādhi for the purpose of clarifying the secrets of all the Tathāgatas and the secret arising of the Jñānakula; he taught the samādhi of the Jñānakula:
"It is four-cornered, with four corners, and joined with the four jewels."
Having visualized [the ground] as being strewn with an ocean of milk, one should commence meditation.
In its center is a great lotus, radiant like crystal and the moon; there, through the union with the clear mandala, one should contemplate the mandala.
Within those masses of flames, one should visualize the form of the Buddha;
one should meditate on it as twenty cubits in height, perfectly circular all around.
In its center, the knower of the ritual procedure should visualize his own auspicious form.
Having abandoned the conceptualizations of self and what belongs to the self, one should commence meditation;
according to the procedure of the Wisdom Family, one should recollect this mantra:
*oṃ sarvatathāgatajñānakulasvabhāvātmako ’ham*.
By this summary of mudrās, one should abandon all evils.
One should meditate upon Vimalodgata, who abounds in ten thousand rays;
according to the ritual procedure, one should visualize the King of Vidyās belonging to the Jñāna family.
One should place [the mantra] rich with subtle, white-rayed flames upon Aditi (?).
One should meditate upon all the *tattvas* [...].
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Vajra-Initiation of All Tathāgatas.
Having made one's own body very firm through the application of the method of the rays,
and by means of the assemblies of Buddha-images characterized by those born of Vajrasattva,
the knower of the ritual should begin; for him, accomplishment is not difficult to attain.
Having made one’s own form motionless according to the procedure of Vajrasattva,
the knower of the ritual should emanate it until it transcends space.
Having rendered the Buddha-form and one’s own form as one through the characteristics of union...
At the time of yogic meditation,
the wise one should project his own form and the form of the Buddha into those [five] locations;
having joined them according to the rule, he should meditate upon Vajrasattva.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Lord of all Tathāgatas:
"The yogi should visualize his own body as being filled with a radiance of garlands of flames;
therein, by means of the vajra-yoga, he should cultivate that very [body] as being indivisible like a vajra."
Having clearly emitted five rays of light, one should visualize the bodhicitta;
having [placed it] in the heart, one should worship all the Buddhas.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Lord of all Tathāgatas.
One should meditate on the maṇḍala, its radiance filled with garlands of flames.
Having filled it with the forms of the Buddhas through the cultivation of mantra, one who is devoted to meditation should,
having formed the image of the Buddha, practice that meditation.
There, one should meditate upon one's own form according to the ritual procedure for the generation of the kalpa;
and there, within the heart, one should cultivate the bodhicitta born of yoga.
The knower of the ritual procedure should then emanate the adorned Vajrasattva.
And within those Vajrasattvas, one should visualize the form of a Buddha;
within the forms of the Buddhas, the knower of the ritual should visualize atomic syllables;
and within all those syllables, one should visualize the forms of the Buddhas.
Within those two syllables, one should visualize one's own form;
through union with the solar mandala, the wise one should meditate on his own form pervading this field with rays of light as far as the limits of space.
One should visualize the vajra-yoga by means of the yoga of the solar disc.
... Within the yogas, one should visualize the image of the Buddha.
And by means of the yogas of the solar discs, one should emanate this world-system.
This field is pervaded by rays as far as it is adorned by space.
Through the yoga of the lunar disk, there is the meditation on the solar disk;
through the yoga of the solar disk, there is the visualization of the form of the Buddha.
"Through the visualization of the Buddha’s image, one visualizes the moon mandala;
through the yoga of the moon mandala, one visualizes the Buddha’s image.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the King of Dharma.
One should conceive of everything through the method of the lotus-yoga;
otherwise, it is not appropriate due to the failure to grasp the meditative cultivation and so forth.
Having clearly visualized the form of the Buddha with a very firm and steady mind, one should proceed.
Having generated the mind of awakening (bodhicitta), one should visualize oneself as the tantra.
This peaceful Vajra method is sharp and possesses a luster like a whetstone;
the knower of the ritual procedure is filled by means of the visualizations of Vajrasattva.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Samantabhadra.
[33] The first chapter, on the ritual arrangement (*vinyāsa*), in the *Mahākalpa* titled *Advayasamatāvijaya*, is completed.
In the center, one should place the image of one's own deity, and on the sides, the women;
having thus grasped them, the knower of the ritual procedure should insert his own vajra there.
"One should worship all the Buddhas in all world-systems with that very [offering]," so said the Blessed One Samantabhadra.
One should visualize five lotuses adorned with garlands of blazing white rays;
in their center, one should place one’s own form, and on the sides, women.
The knower of the ritual procedure should emanate these as arising from one’s own semen and so forth.
The meditation on the space-element completely filled with the forms of the Buddhas.
This concludes the second chapter, the Samādhi of the Knowledge Family, in the *Mahākalparāja* entitled *Advayasamatāvijaya*.
When this has been performed, the logic that is difficult for those who know logic to grasp is as follows:
having made one's own form very firm, one intent on meditation should project it.
He shall be endowed with a perfect body, radiant and pleasing to behold;
at the mere sight of him, women are filled with delight—of this there is no doubt.
One should visualize this field as being completely filled with Vajrasattvas.
"Having made the image of the Buddha firm, one should strike it down with a vajra.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the indivisible triple-vajra.
[55] The third chapter, the Samādhi of the Family of the Compendium, from the *Advayasamatāvijaya-mahākalparāja*, is completed.
Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi spoke the chapter on the meditative absorption of the Dharma family:
"Everything that has been taught here regarding the great maṇḍala must be performed;
one who knows the ritual procedure should undertake the visualization of the Dharma family."
Having abandoned all extremes of conceptual construction through the characteristics of the union with the Dharma,
one should recite the various mantras and contemplate the yoga of all:
*Oṃ, I am of the nature of the wisdom of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas.*
Having recited [the mantra], the knower of the ritual procedure, through the yoga of the great commitment (*mahāsamaya*),
should generate all phenomena and then not conceptualize them as non-existent.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Lokeśvara.
The wheel is proclaimed in the Jñānakula; the sword is remembered in the Dharmakula;
the thunderbolt is renowned in the Saṃgrahakula; and the trident is remembered in the Kāmakula.
[67] The fourth chapter, the section on the meditative absorption of the Dharma-maṇḍala, within the Great Kalpa of the Victory over Non-duality and Equality, is completed.

Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, having established all those Tathāgatas within his own great vajra and having caused them to enter the Jñānakula and so forth through the yoga of the knowledge of that great maṇḍala, and having stabilized them and established their abiding in the form of his own image within those great maṇḍalas, he joined the Great Image with the forms of the gods of the Great Devas and spoke the samādhi of the Kāmakula:
"Everything should be performed exactly in that manner through the yoga of the great maṇḍala.
One who knows the ritual procedure should begin; otherwise, one should not meditate at all."
One should recollect the mantra-veda according to the ritual procedure of the Kāma family:
"Oṃ, I am of the nature of the knowledge of desire."
Having passed beyond eight hundred cubits, one should visualize Mahāpadma;
having produced the image of Viṣṇu, one should meditate upon the Buddhas and others therein.
Having generated the image of a Buddha, one should pervade this [universe] with images of Brahmā;
having generated the image of the Dharma, one should pervade this with images of Viṣṇu;
and having made all the images firm, one should pervade them with images resembling the flames of desire.
The knower of the ritual procedure should expand [the visualization] throughout the world-system in all directions.
Having transcended [the limit of] one cubit, there is the meditation upon the forms of Brahmā.
Having generated that within the heart, one should meditate upon the forms of the Buddhas.
"One who knows the ritual procedure should visualize the image within the image.
Thus spoke the Blessed One Kāmārcis.
"Having transcended [the distance of] one cubit, one visualizes the image of Viṣṇu."
Having generated that [deity] within the heart, one should visualize the form of a Buddha.
Within all those Buddha-forms, the knower of the ritual procedure should emanate a form resembling the flames of desire, adorned with playful ornaments.
"As many as are the conjunctions of forms, so many are the women," thus spoke the Blessed One, the Flame of Desire.
Having produced the form through the yoga of the family maṇḍala, one should meditate upon it.
One who knows the ritual procedure should meditate with a concentrated mind upon the initial yoga;
having made the space-element remembered as being completely filled, the wise one,
having discerned it by way of color and form, should cause that [deity] to descend while remaining in meditative equipoise.

The mantra-practitioner who knows the ritual procedure should bestow an image in the form of the Goddess, possessing a radiance equal to that of a Buddha, according to the proper rule; otherwise, there is no accomplishment at all. The practitioner who knows the ritual procedure should likewise visualize his own form as being in the likeness of the Goddess.
Except for those who are Vajrasattvas, [one should practice] with semen and so forth produced according to the ritual rules.
Having fashioned one's own image, adorned with playful ornaments through the yoga of the sharp [faculty],
the knower of the procedure should perform battle with the goddess there and meditate upon it.
The knower of the ritual, having joined the vajras and lotuses produced according to the rules,
should generate the family-form and worship it with his own seminal essences;
otherwise, the deities of the Jina-lotus families will certainly not be accomplished.
The deities proclaimed in the Vajrapāṇi family do not attain accomplishment at all [without this].
This must be performed during the four junctions (saṃdhyā), both at the beginning and at the end in every way.
Otherwise, those born of the lotus and thunderbolt families of the Jinas will certainly not attain accomplishment.
Having produced the Mother-image, which possesses a radiance equal to various rays of light,
one should cause even the triple world to pervade one's own image through the yoga of the flames of desire.
Through union with the four sisters, the image becomes like the flames of desire.
One should cause the concentrated practitioner to recite by means of the yoga of the reflected image (*bimba*).
Having clearly visualized the Brahma-image as resembling yellow filaments (*kiñjalka*),
the one who knows the ritual procedure, having fashioned the Buddha-images, should then empower them.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Holder of Dharma.
The fifth chapter, on the Samādhi of the Family of Desire, in the *Advayasamatāvijaya-mahākalparāja*, is completed.

Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, having established all the Tathāgatas within his own maṇḍala and entered his own meditative absorption, spoke the chapter on the Supreme Knowledge of the Pledge of All Siddhis from the Great Kalpa of the Victory of Non-dual Equality.
The wise person should not form conceptual constructions regarding any desires;
one should never revile the mind, which is the slayer of all Buddhas.
One who contradicts all Buddhas [is characterized by] the marks of those who speak with pleasant words.
The mind must certainly not be made firm; otherwise, O Goddess, it would be so.
That which is the substance of all Buddhas, unarisen and consisting of qualities, that mind must be made very firm; one should contemplate it within women and the like.
The Great Vidyā named Locanā is the sovereign of the three worlds;
having made those women her own, he who knows the ritual of the Jñānakula should enjoy them in every way and should then proceed to slay them together with me.
For the sake of gathering [disciples], one should always perform the destruction of the auspiciousness of living beings;
within the family of Dharma, one should always apply passion by means of passion;
and one should always speak falsehoods in the presence of the family of the Kāmārci.
In all cases, this must be performed in this way; otherwise, it will not succeed at all.
Having visualized the form of the Buddha, one should visualize him within the heart.
Everything should be done exactly thus; otherwise, it will not come to pass.
By harming the family of gnosis (*jñānakula*), one is reborn among the Tuṣita gods;
by harming the family of Dharma (*dharmakula*), one is born in Sukhāvatī.
Through the distinctions of the families of Dharma and so forth, that which is called "attraction" (*saṃgraha*) has been proclaimed.
Through the destruction of the family of the fire of desire, there arises the origin of the three realms and so forth.
Without the body, they do not abide; yet for the embodied one, they abide.
That which is nourished should be explained; it is born within all phenomena.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Lord of all Tathāgatas:
"I am firm like a vajra for the infinite realm of sentient beings; having delivered them from the bonds of existence, I shall establish them by the command of the Buddhas."
By these methods of the Dharma, which arise from the excellence of all-knowledge of the Buddhas,
the gathering of sentient beings could not otherwise be accomplished;
for they consist of the great accumulation of wisdom and skillful means, the perfection of insight.
By constantly unifying the mind, one attains the compendium of the Dharma;
the great contemplation of the bodhicitta does not have the characteristics of a vajra or similar objects.
For this is the essential collection of all gnoses.
In this world, the perfections are the firm consorts of the Buddhas;
through union with these, characterized by their respective attributes, one attains Buddhahood— the experience of sound, smell, taste, and so forth, according to one's capacity.
One should visualize one's own form in the center through the yoga of the Buddha;
having made it filled with masses of radiant flames, one should cause it to enter the heart.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Holder of Dharma.
In the family known as Saṃgraha, it is proclaimed that he is born from the Great Drama;
having recognized the marvel therein, his slaying is indeed recorded there.
Furthermore, in the state of Mahāmudrā, the four castes of men are also mentioned.
Having performed [this] through the yoga of the pledge, one should meditate upon it with a concentrated mind.
For the mind of all sentient beings is a great excellence of intrinsic nature;
yet inferior beings speak of it as being mounted upon the pledge of conceptual construction.
That body is neither stained by merit nor by demerit;
having understood this according to the proper principle, one should not conceive of it otherwise.
[93] The sixth chapter, titled "The Supreme Knowledge of the Samaya of All Siddhis," from the *Advayasamatāvijaya*, the Great King of Mahākalpas, is completed.
Furthermore, the mantra practitioner who meditates four times a day for two months should cultivate [the visualization] in delightful,
secluded, and solitary places.

The practitioner of the vow may eat fish, meat, and so forth, and even drink [them] with clarified butter; he may also consume what has been stolen—provided that the practitioner acts in this manner. One who knows the procedure for the image of the Buddha sees him directly.
One should know [reality] by means of one's own reflection alone; such a person does not hear sounds at all.
For him, no twofold mind arises again and again. Whatever one should cultivate through meditative realization, that alone it shall become, and not otherwise.
Having generated the yoga of the pure maṇḍala and so forth, one should meditate upon that;
having fully generated the yoga of the Lord, one should meditate with a concentrated mind.
Otherwise, no accomplishment whatsoever arises regarding the phenomena of activity.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Bodhicitta.
[103] In the Great King of Great Kalpas, the Victory over Non-dual Equality, this is the seventh chapter, the Compendium of Primordial Gnosis.

Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, having caused all those Tathāgatas to enter his own pores, entered the meditative absorption named "The Empowerment Arising from the Knowledge of All Samayas. As soon as the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi had entered that absorption, all those Tathāgatas transformed their own forms into female forms and emerged from those very same pores.
Grasping the neck and other parts with the hand, one should place the feet there;
the meditator should insert his own vajra and contemplate it with the characteristics of the two flowers and so forth.
Through union with the moon-maṇḍala, he should cause the semen to fall therein.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajradhara:
"Having filled the entire realm of space, one should meditate by means of that very [mantra].
Worship with the four flowers and so forth is indeed prescribed therein."
One who is devoted to worship should perform worship through the union with the five types of offering-presents;
one should offer fragrance, form, taste, and touch by that very means in every way.
[This is] the origin of all Buddhas and the wise Vajrasattvas.
Satisfying and worshiping are declared to be the same as pleasing;
by this, the accomplishment of mantras arises for practitioners.
For the sake of achieving illumination and nourishment, one shall attain Buddhahood and other such states.
For this is the true nature (*dharmatā*) of the Buddhas, provided it is the syllable of the true nature itself;
otherwise, the attainment of Buddhahood and so forth can never be achieved.
One must never perform unwholesome acts of mind, nor should one ever practice censure.
For this is the collection of syllables of the true nature (*dharmatā*) of all Buddhas. Those others who would enjoy a woman here according to their desire,
should worship her according to reality through the yoga of the solar disc.
Generosity, ethical discipline, patience, and likewise firm vigor—
these the wise mantra-practitioner should consecrate according to the ritual procedure.
Having properly recited his own mantra, he should join it with the word "candram" (the moon).
The mantra-practitioner should again cause [the seed-syllable] to enter briefly into that vajra;
he should form the pericarp itself, with the visualization of jewels on its sides.
Their colors should be understood in brief according to the distinctions of the families.
One who knows the ritual procedure should always honor women of ten years of age in the Jñānakula;
in the [tradition] called Saṃgraha, one should always [honor] those twelve years of age who possess virtue and splendor.
The practitioner of mantra should always begin with a sixteen-year-old girl in the family known as Dharma;
one should worship a twenty-year-old girl in the entire Kāmārca family.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Maṇḍala of the Samaya of all Tathāgatas.
One should maintain her until she reaches twelve years of age, as long as the semen is retained.
In brief, whatever is desired should be performed according to the Dharma and in accordance with the proper method.
She should be adorned with various ornaments and decorated with garlands, wreaths, and the like.
Having first performed [the visualization of] Vairocana and the others, one should then commence the worship.

Sandalwood and saffron are prescribed according to the specific division of the *kula* for the ritual action; the mandala should be made with that very substance, which is exceedingly beautiful and endowed with splendor.
"In brief, all that is to be done should be performed in such a way that no differentiation arises;
for if there were differentiation, even for that Buddha, [the goal] would not be accomplished.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, whose mind is the mind of all Tathāgatas.
Having adorned seven maidens who are endowed with all auspicious marks,
aged between sixteen and eighteen years,
neither too tall nor too short, neither emaciated nor of low birth.
One should not practice with a maiden who is not of such a kind; otherwise, it will certainly not succeed.
Having taken her, one who knows the ritual procedure should practice by means of the accomplishments of reality (*tattva*).
When the first watch has passed and the second has arrived,
the practitioner who possesses the means to be accomplished shall indeed achieve accomplishment in reality;
even for one who has committed the five acts of immediate retribution, when half a watch has elapsed.
The practitioner is constantly perfected, empowered by Vajrapāṇi;
having become like the Lord of the Family, he shall wander throughout the entire world-system with countless millions of women for the sake of attaining the realization of accomplishment.
By means of that activity, he who has arisen as Vajrapāṇi causes the atoms of Mount Sumeru to perform the task for the sake of sentient beings.
[116] The eighth chapter, the Secret Worship for the Great Accomplishment of All Samayas, in the *Mahākalpamahārāja* titled *Advayasamatāvijaya*, is completed.
One may slay incalculable numbers of all beings through the yoga of reality;
Buddhahood is attained in this very life— of this there is no doubt.
One who, through the yoga of gnosis, causes ten million Buddhas to be slain,
will achieve accomplishment in this very life and attain the state of Vajrasattva.

For the mind of all sentient beings is pure, peaceful, and luminous; it is called "mind" because it is unstained by various phenomena. Through the cultivation of reality, one who knows the ritual procedures should truly enjoy the consort of the Buddha.
Otherwise, all mantras that give rise to auspiciousness will not succeed at all.
Therefore, the mantra-practitioner should especially extract the supreme *gaṇas*.
Otherwise, Vajrasattva and those who bring about auspiciousness will not be pleased.
One should undertake enjoyment in all matters concerning enjoyment;
otherwise, if that foolish soul acts differently, they will be cooked in the vicinity of the Avīci hell.
One might as well devour one's own self or drink alcohol oneself.
One should indeed offer [these] to all the Buddhas; then they will certainly be swiftly accomplished.
One should always eat human flesh, or one should drink oil oneself;
or the knower of the ritual, being devoted to consumption, should consume even excrement and urine.
One should not offer to the Buddhas and others anything arising from the opening of a wound;
rather, having created great clouds of flowers and perfumes, one should present everything according to its true nature.
The practitioner of mantra must always strive with diligence to be free from disgust.
"This indeed is the pledge (samaya) declared for all Buddhas by Jñānabuddhi. Thus spoke the Blessed One, the executor of the commands of all Tathāgatas:
"The mantra-practitioner should always [draw] the mandala with feces and urine, each time."
Or one of steady mind should perform the practice of lying down and so forth;
having produced a square [mandala] filled with feces and urine,
one should fill one's own body within it up to the tip of the nose.
For the Blessed Buddha is indeed Bhaga; therefore, passion is not defiled.
As for the other three in brief, they are indeed different and not established in that [Bhaga]. One who knows the ritual procedure should cause others to be made and should employ them accordingly.
Impelled by the wheel of gnosis, he shall attain vast accomplishment;
whether acting for himself or for another, he does not fail to apply it according to reality.
He shall certainly not fail to attain Buddhahood as long as space endures.
I am Avīci; I am the terrible; I am suffering; I am happiness.
I am hatred, and likewise I am delusion; I am established in passion.
[121] Thus ends the ninth chapter, the supreme secret section titled "The Awakening to the Gnosis of All Tathāgatas," within the *Mahākalpa-mahārāja* known as the *Advayasamatāvijaya*.
Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, once again for the sake of attaining the gnosis of all Tathāgatas, spoke the secret commitment (*samaya*) of the hearts of all Vajrasattvas:
"One should not pay homage even to Arhats, nor should one pay homage to monks;
one should not even mention paying homage to those who have attained the Buddhahood of the Buddhas."
If anyone should transgress this, even if it be Vajrasattva himself,
[the teacher] shall speak the *bodhicitta* while [the disciple's] head is split into seven parts.
Having placed the *liṅga* in the *bhaga*, one should mutter the mantra again and again.
Having generated Vajrasattva, one should meditate upon him within one's own form.
This reality of the Buddha-Ācāryas must always be guarded with particular care;
otherwise, the Ācāryas will certainly not attain Buddhahood.
Having clearly visualized one's own form in accordance with the reality of the ritual action,
and having generated the thought of awakening (bodhicitta), one should then meditate upon the Buddha as the preceptor.
I am accomplished as the self of Vajrasattva, empowered by the Vajrasattvas;
I always ferry [beings] across to the vajra state in the ground of the wisdom-dharma.
I am accomplished through the wisdom-vajra, empowered by that which is called Amṛta and the rest.
"I, the auspicious one, roam through the atoms of space," thus spoke the Blessed One, Mahāvajradhara.

Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi again spoke the commitment (*samaya*) of all Tathāgatas, called the "Empowerment of the Reality of the Purification of the Mantras of the Body, Speech, and Mind Wisdom of All Tathāgatas."
Mind is said to be the vajra; its cultivation is born from Vajrasattva.
Having cultivated that mind, one should cause it to enter the wisdom-vajra.
For the sake of purifying the intrinsic nature of the vajra, there is the examination of the speech-vajra.

Through the manifestation of pure gnosis, one should visualize the purity of body and speech; one who knows the ritual procedure should consecrate the indivisible vajra-body, radiant with the empowerment of the vajra,
by means of the nature of the Buddha-body.
By this, one attains awakening when empowered by these vajras;
one who knows the ritual procedure shall attain Buddhahood right here within six months.
All that which arises from the vajra is unstained by phenomena born of passion.
Having thus performed the rite of reality, one attains all accomplishments;
whatever happiness belongs to the Buddhas and teachers, that same happiness belongs to the practitioners of reality.
The mantra-practitioner should wander like a lion, free from all fear;
he brings about the state of Buddhahood in this very life at that very moment.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Samaya of all Tathāgatas.
[124] In the *Advayasamatāvijaya*, the Great King of Great Kalpas, this is the tenth chapter, the Chapter on the Samaya.

Then all the Tathāgatas, having assembled in the assembly, honored the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi with cloud-like arrays of offerings of the body, speech, mind, and gnosis of all the Tathāgatas, and spoke thus: "O Blessed One, speak the reality of the supreme great maṇḍala—
the meditation that brings about all accomplishments, the supreme maṇḍala of meditation."

Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, having heard the request of all the Tathāgatas, entered the samādhi called "The Empowerment of the Vajra-Samaya of All Tathāgatas" and proclaimed this great maṇḍala, which bestows the knowledge of the accomplishments of all samayas:
"Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme great maṇḍala,
which resembles vajra-wisdom and illuminates the awakening of the Buddhas."
One should visualize the element of space completely filled with all the Buddhas; worship with the seminal essence (śukra) is proclaimed as the meditation by that means.
The meditation maṇḍala called "Accomplishment of All Samayas" is completed.
One should visualize the goddess Kuleśvarī in the corner, in her proper place.
The mantra-practitioner should visualize that delightful woman, endowed with all the characteristics of a beautiful female, adorned with feminine ornaments, and possessing eyes both red and not-red;
and at all the entrances, he should likewise visualize the Vidyā Aparājitā.
Standing in the *ālīḍha* posture, she captivates the realm of the three worlds.
Within all those very forms, one should visualize Vajrasattva.
By means of the supreme five qualities of sensory pleasure, the Buddha-teacher should always [serve] them.
The offering must always be performed; in this way they are satisfied, and not otherwise.
Having generated one's own semen, it is known as the worship and the generation.
One should indeed visualize the space-element (*khadhātu*) as completely filled with those forms.
Having understood the wish-fulfilling trees, the great jewels, and the excellent purification of the *cintāmaṇi* according to the divisions of the families, one should visualize their colors; then,
one should receive the empowerment by means of those images as prescribed.
Then, one who knows the ritual procedure should visualize the vases;
one should visualize them being worshipped by all [deities], such as the images of the Buddhas.
One should visualize oneself as equally consecrated by these characteristics of union.
Buddhahood is attained in this very life, right here; there is no doubt about this.
This concludes the eleventh chapter, the Chapter on Great Meditation, in the *Mahākalpamahārāja*, the *Advayasamatāvijaya*.
Oṃ, svāhā to the one arisen from the wisdom of all Tathāgatas!
Oṃ, svāhā to the one arisen from the knowledge of gathering! Oṃ, svāhā to the one arisen from the knowledge of phenomena!
Oṃ, svāhā to the one arisen from desire and knowledge!
The twelfth chapter, titled "The Maṇḍala of Meditative Concentration," concerning the generation of the Great Beings (mahāsattva), is completed.

Then the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi again entered the meditative absorption named "The Vajra Empowerment Arising from the Samaya that Fulfills All Aspirations," and proclaimed this great maṇḍala of the great samaya-attainment:
"Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the supreme great maṇḍala."
Resembling vajra-wisdom, it is known as the "Great Accomplishment. With a new, well-prepared, well-measured, and beautiful thread, the wise one should delineate the mandala according to his ability.
It is square, with four gates, adorned with four archways,
provided with four [boundary] lines, and decorated with silk ribbons, garlands, and strings of flowers;
[it is likewise adorned] at all the corner sections and at the junctions of the gates and projections.
One should trace the outer maṇḍala, inlaid with vajra-jewels;
it should always be constructed according to the ritual as a triple-layered structure in brief.
To the east, the one who knows the procedure should establish that which is called "Knowledge."
To the south, one should always diligently perform that which is called "attraction" (saṃgraha).
To the north, one should always perform the "family of Dharma" according to the prescribed rule.
Or, the practitioner of mantra may draw the "family of all desires" as the third.
To the east [he should place] the Buddha Bhagavān Jayoṣṇīṣa with a white parasol,
and the Great Vidyā Locanā and Urṇā nearby;
to the south, Vajradhara known as Amṛta, who possesses great power.
One should station Māmakī and Vajramuṣṭi nearby;
to the north of the Blessed One, one should place Padmadhara, who brings auspiciousness,
and Bhṛkuṭītaraṅga.

One who knows the ritual procedure should draw the great vidyā named Pāṇḍarā and Bhṛkuṭī; there, in the center, he should draw the tongue of the vidyā. Furthermore, within all the mudrās, one should visualize a five-pronged trident.
In the third mandala, the preceptor may at his discretion paint [the deities] together with their consorts;
however, at all the gates, he should paint Vajrasphoṭa and the others.
In all directions, he should install the world-protectors according to the rule.
In the eastern direction, Indra, the king of the gods, the gods of the desire realm (*kāmāvacara*), and the Śuddhāvāsa gods are to be depicted.
In the southeastern direction, all the great seers possessing the five superknowledges (*pañcābhijña*) and the fire deities are to be depicted.
In the southern direction, Yama, the lord of the hungry ghosts (*preta*), together with the seven Mothers, is to be depicted.
In the southwestern direction are the Lord of Pretas and all spirits;
in the western direction is Varuṇa, the Lord of Nāgas, and all Nāgas;
in the northwestern direction is Vāyu and all Vidyādharas.
In the northern direction is Kuvera, the lord of wealth;
all the yakṣas, and Īśāna, the lord of spirits, [preside over] everything.
The installation of the water-pot (kalaśa) and other rites should be performed according to the prescribed rule.

The wise one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of all the kings and deities. Having performed the procedure for worship with perfumes, flowers, and other offerings, he should satisfy them with pleasing and appropriate means; in this way they are satisfied, and not otherwise.
One who knows the procedure for the secret worship should first offer fish, meat, and so forth to them; he should arrange these at the four gates.
Having taken that semen, he should then present it to all.
One should satisfy her repeatedly according to the rules of the Vidyā-naya.
The wise practitioner should first offer an oblation to Priyaṅkāra;
then, one who knows the ritual procedure should present the second to Hārītī.

The mantra-practitioner should especially offer the third [oblation] to all the Buddhas; then the fire-offering ritual (homakarma) should be performed as taught by the proponents of reality (tattvavādins). At that time, he should bestow upon the disciples the rite of consecration (abhiṣeka).
Having generated this family through the principle of dependent origination for one whose mind is otherwise,
the Buddha-teacher should always explain this method to him as the practice of Vajrasattva, wherein the remainder is the Buddha.
This is the commitment of all Buddhas who traverse the three paths:
their great empowerment extends as far as the limits of space.
This specific teaching is also spoken by me; this too is my manifestation.
Relying upon the jewel-like wish-fulfilling gem, I have been consecrated by those born of reality.
Whatever sentient beings hear my name, or even behold me,
shall attain the supreme stage within seven future births.
Just as the Buddha-teacher, the ocean of wisdom, remains so,
the Buddhas always worship that great sage who knows reality;
then the Buddha-teacher acts toward his own disciple as has been described.
Having bestowed the five pledges,
one should diligently explain the great pledge-maṇḍala, the reality-knowledge maṇḍala of all Buddhas,
and how you, O practitioner, have arisen like a wish-fulfilling gem.
The Great Samaya Maṇḍala is completed.

Vajrapāṇi questioned the Blessed One Mahāvairocana. Then the Blessed One Mahāvairocana proclaimed the method of knowledge for beginners, titled "The Supreme Accomplishment of the Samaya of All Tathāgatas."
This is that which fulfills all hopes of all mantras;
this is declared to be the primordial meditation, which should be cultivated with diligence.

The thirteenth chapter, concerning the rites for beginners in the method of *vidyā*, within the *Mahākalparāja* titled *Advayasamatāvijaya*, is completed. Then the Blessed One, Mahāvairocana, proclaimed the purification of the secret method of *vidyā* for all mantras.
The fourteenth chapter, on the ritual activities of the vidyās, in the Great Kalparāja titled *Advayasamatāvijaya*, is completed.
Having visualized the form of the Buddha, wearing a crown of matted hair,
one should generate the Buddha-teacher and cause him to enter one's heart.
Having meditated upon the supreme mudrā of one’s own mantra, one should place it within the heart.
This reality (tattva) has been proclaimed for the times of drinking and eating, for the modes of enjoyment, and for activities such as [perceiving] fragrance, form, and so forth.

One who knows the ritual procedure should always offer one's own happiness to the Buddha-teacher through union with the deity; otherwise, there is no accomplishment at all. This is that which fulfills all hopes for all mantras.
The reality that brings about the accomplishment of mantras is the secret of all the omniscient ones;
likewise, it involves the killing of all beings, the seizing of others' property,
the service of all the dexterous ones, and the practice of one's own form and so forth.
This is that which accomplishes the buddha-knowledge of all buddhas;
it was emanated by Vajrasattva through the means of accomplishing vajra-knowledge.
One who knows the ritual procedure should draw the disciple’s mother, his excellent wife, his sister, and his daughter within the center of the mandala, and there he should enjoy them.
Then the Blessed One proclaimed the means of accomplishment (*sādhana*) and the secondary means of accomplishment (*upasādhana*):
"Having become one who consumes fish, wine, and food, and being devoted to the secret worship and so forth,
wherever the mind and the mantra abide, there one should perform the yoga of the Great Pledge (*mahāsamaya-yoga*)."
Then, being free from waves [of mental agitation], he should begin with one month; by that, his attainments such as Buddhahood will be accomplished.
Having first recited [the mantra] for six months in his own place, such as a mountain cave,
the practitioner, constantly empowered by Vajrasattva, accomplishes [his goal].
Whether she be a celestial maiden, a nāginī, a human woman, or even an asurī,
one should commence the secret worship by attracting her according to the prescribed rule,
in secluded and delightful places, in mountain caves, or in forests.
There, having drawn [the deity] forth, one should enjoy [him] with the five excellent qualities of sensory desire.
Having caused the pledge (samaya) to be heard, as impelled by vajra-wisdom,
the knower of the ritual procedure may even draw forth Vajrasattva himself.
"Aho! Indeed, I am the essence of the system of all mantras;
having attained Buddhahood within six months, all indeed become Buddhas."
Then the Blessed One entered the meditative absorption named Viśuddhavajra and uttered this Mahāvajragāndhārī:

Oṃ! Come, come, O Blessed One, Great Vajragāndhārī! By the truth of the Three Jewels, draw near, draw near! [I invoke] Baladeva, Maheśvara, Garuḍa, Viṣṇu, Kumāra, Brahmā, Indra, Candra, Āditya, Yama, Varuṇa, Kuvera, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Virūḍhaka, Virūpākṣa, Ṣaṭkarṇa, Bhṛṅgiriṭi, Nāyaka, Vināyaka, Pāñcika, Lohaka, the Goddess Ṣaṣṭhī, Koṭagiri, Oṃkārī, Durgā, Kātyāyanī, Caṇḍakātyāyanī, and Mahākātyāyanī.

I shall cause [the goddesses] to turn toward me quickly—having seized them twice, *hulu* twice, *culu* twice, *mulu* twice, blow twice, *raṅga* twice, fill twice, enter twice—the Āiśānī, the Kālī in the southwest, Mahākālī, Vajrakālī, Yaśasvinī, Sakālī, Bhadrakālī in the southeast, Halikāvartī in the northwest, Śakti, Śatākṣī, Indrāṇī, Brahmāṇī, Kauverī, Māheśvarī, Vaiṣṇavī, Subhagā, Cāmuṇḍā, Raudrī, Vārāhī, Kauverī, and whoever else stands by me. O Blessed One!
Mahāvajragāndhāri, the accomplished Caṇḍavajrapāṇi, commands: hrī haḥ haḥ haḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
The sixteenth chapter, the Compendium of All Mantras, is completed.
The chapter on the expulsion of all Tathāgatas is completed.
One should never directly behold the happiness of one's teachers;
for that foolish-minded person who does so is then tormented in the Raurava hell.
Whatever the teacher seeks, that indeed one should offer to him;
otherwise, there will be no accomplishment for you... [the truth].
One should present a maiden to the virtuous teachers as a wife for their disciples.
Or he may give his sister; he will succeed, there is no doubt in this.
For one distinguished by such qualities, [the result] shall manifest within six months.
Otherwise, if that deluded soul is cooked in the vicinity of Avīci,
then when someone is born possessing these qualities, he becomes a source of merit.
The teacher should not reveal the tantras to him in such a manner at the outset.

Having thus attained the reality of the Dharma with a purified self and remaining established in the ritual procedure, the teacher may then reveal them; one attains success quickly in this way, and not otherwise.
The eighteenth chapter, on the propitiation of Vajrasattva, the secret of the Tathāgatas, is completed.
One should recite the mantra whose limbs are not deficient; it certainly succeeds within a month.
Having performed service and so forth, one should practice the mantra-sādhana;
having maintained the vow (saṃvara) therein, one certainly attains success, and not otherwise. Having obtained the ritual procedure, the mantra practiced by the practitioner attains success.
Therefore, the mantra-practitioner should especially observe the vow;
whatever vow has been proclaimed, that very one the observer of the vow must protect. Otherwise, he shall remain in the Avīci hell for as long as space exists.
One should maintain the vow of the master according to the rules for as long as one lives;
for such a person, Buddhahood— the abode of the entire universe— is accomplished.
The twenty-first chapter, on the propitiation of all mantras, is completed.
One should not despise excrement and urine, for they bestow happiness upon all sentient beings;
they alone are King Vajradhara, the foremost of all, the Lord of the World.
One born from the nine wounds should never be despised;
he alone is the King who holds the Vajra, the foremost of all, the Lord of the World. Indeed, passion must not be despised, for it bestows all happiness and welfare.
He alone is the King Vajradhara, the foremost of all, the Lord of the World;
for hatred is not to be despised, due to the awakening of vajra-wisdom.
He alone is the King Vajradhara, the foremost of all, the Lord of the World.
Whether it be a princess, a minister’s daughter, or even a daughter of a Buddha—
if one should take her and enjoy her until the mind is satisfied;
The first is proclaimed as the possession by the pillar;
the second is called the stage; and the third is the supreme, divine one.
And the fourth [initiation] was proclaimed by Vajrapāṇi in the Noble Land;
having become naked with disheveled hair and wearing grotesque, formidable ornaments.
One should oneself write his name using charcoal from a cremation ground;
having recited [the mantra] one thousand times, even a Buddha will certainly be seized.
One who knows the procedure for wet clothing, having set out with a mind of wrath, [should act].
Having stepped upon the feet of a *liṅga*, even a Buddha certainly perishes. Placing one's feet upon Viṣṇu, the Daityas, and the foremost of gods,
one who knows the ritual procedure may destroy even the triple world within seven days.
The nineteenth chapter, the Great Secret Chapter, is completed.
Excrement and urine are not to be despised, for they bestow happiness upon all sentient beings;
they are indeed King Vajradhara, the foremost of all, the Lord of the World.
That which arises from the nine orifices should never be despised;
for he is the King who holds all vajras, the foremost of all, the Lord of the World. Indeed, passion must not be despised, as it bestows all happiness and benefit.
For he is the King Vajradhara, the foremost of all, the Lord of the World;
indeed, hatred is not to be despised, for it awakens the vajra-wisdom.
He alone is the King Vajradhara, the foremost of all, the Lord of the World.
Delusion indeed is not to be despised, for it awakens all-encompassing knowledge;
it is itself the King who holds peace, the Buddha, the abode of Vairocana.
Suffering and pleasure indeed are not to be despised, for they are the Teacher as long as life lasts.
He alone is King Śāntadhara, the Buddha Vairocanālaya;
one must not disregard dharma or adharma, nor the teacher, for as long as life lasts.
He alone is King Vajradhara, the sovereign of all, the teacher of reality.
The realm of sentient beings must never be despised at any time throughout one's life;
he alone is the King Vajradhara, the foremost of all, the Lord of the World.
One must never harbor contempt for them in any activity throughout the duration of one's life.
He himself is the lotus-bearing king, the foremost of all, the Lord of the World.

Then, having heard the syllable—the *dharmatā* of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas—all the Tathāgatas were struck with wonder and spoke thus to all the Vajradharas: "O noble son, this is truly marvelous! For even those who are sovereigns over the wisdom of the Omniscient One do not know it; how much less so others?"
One who knows the ritual procedure should perform the fire offering (homa) if he desires supreme accomplishment;
established in the meditative absorption on the secret reality, he should undertake the various types of fire offerings.

For pacification (*śāntika*), the mandala is circular; for enrichment (*pauṣṭika*), it is four-cornered; for malevolent rites (*abhicāra*), it has a triangular point; and for subjugation (*vaśya*), it is shaped like a bow. One should meditate upon the gentle [deity] situated in the center of the fire as being like nectar.
In that very place, one should meditate upon the form of the deity as one's own true nature;
oneself as the form of the Lord— this is what arises from the Vajra Way.
The twentieth chapter, the "Chapter on the Wish-Fulfilling Gem of the Mantras of All Tathāgatas," in the *Advayasamatāvijaya*, the Great Kalparāja, is completed.
The twenty-first chapter, titled "The Compendium of All Mantras," from the *Advayasamatāvijaya-mahākalparāja*, is completed.
The Bodhisattvas, having attained the nature of awakening, are fearless;
their enjoyments fill the realm of space and are established in the awakening of the Vajra.
In phenomena that are without characteristics, conceptual proliferation does not exist;
through the wisdom of the vajra-nature, they are as stainless as space.
The twenty-second chapter, titled "The Vajra of the Nature of the Complete Purity of the Body, Speech, and Mind of All Tathāgatas," is finished.
The Great King of Ritual Manuals named *Āryādvayasamatāvijaya* is completed.
